messages:
maria: Heads-up — noticed spike of preemptible evictions in us-west-2 over last 10m. If this continues we'll need a live plan for routing and preserving SLAs for paid tiers.

jamal: Seen it. PVs showed 30% churn on p3-preemptible yesterday at 02:00 UTC. Is this the same wave? :eyes: 

sophie: Yup. multiregion telemetry looks correlated with a cloud maintenance window. us-west-2 first, then ap-southeast-1. infra-bot also flagged higher reboots.

infra-bot: ALERT: preemptible_eviction_rate > 0.25 on pool:p3-preemptible-usw2 (1m)

alex: Proposal: implement an "escape hatch" routing rule chain:
- 1) fast local fallback to warm on-demand in same AZ for gold customers up to 40% traffic
- 2) if local on-demand exhausted, route to remote region (latency check, metric: 99p added latency) for dedicated customers
- 3) for free/low-tier, degrade to quantized model variant with async long-polling option

maria: +1 on escape hatch. Can we add a short-circuit so the high-priority path never triggers cross-region unless backoff fails 3x? Don't want flapping.

jamal: Agreed. Also add a token-leaky bucket per-tenant to prevent warm pool exhaustion. config snippet:
```
routing:
  - match: tier == "gold"
    attempt_order: [local_on_demand, remote_on_demand, quantized_async]
    circuit_breaker: {max_failures:3, cooldown:30s}
  - match: tier == "free"
    attempt_order: [quantized_sync, quantized_async, best_effort_cpu]
```

sophie: We should also pre-warm a small standby of warm VMs for top 50 tenants during known maintenance windows. Cost hit but saves SLA penalties.

erin: On cost — warm on-demand for top tenants at 10% capacity costs about +16% per-hour but cuts p99 by ~220ms in our sims. For lower tiers, quantized 4-bit reduces cost 2.5x but increases hallucination risk slightly.

alex: Also consider shunting long-running requests to CPU-only fallback with notification to customer (async job). Implementation: accept, return job_id, process batch on cpu-pool.

maria: Good. Can we add observability knobs: a per-route "degrade_score" that tracks quality drift after model-variant fallback? We need automatic rollback if error/quality delta > threshold.

jamal: I'll prototype a small metric: degrade_score = (bleu_drop * 0.6) + (latency_penalty*0.4). Alert threshold 0.2.

sophie: One more — network egress spikes when cross-region failover happens. We need quota bump or use compressed payloads during failover (gzip) + smaller beam sizes.

erin: I'll run cost calc for three scenarios and post numbers in this thread later today.

alex: I'll draft the routing policy PR and a canary run with 5 tenants tomorrow. tagging @maria for review.

maria: Thanks. If infra-bot triggers again, temporarily enable `escape_hatch: true` and let's watch the metrics. :rocket:

infra-bot: METRIC-UPDATE: escape_hatch toggled false -> true by jamal at 1862003972

jamal: Toggled on during the maintenance window. early signals look stable.

maria: Great. Follow up doc in #eng-infra-playbooks with runbook steps and cost sheet.

sophie: noted. will add prewarm schedule and compression toggle.

erin: posting cost numbers in 20m.

alex: PR: https://git.internal.redwood/infra/routing/pulls/312 :eyes: 

maria: Closing the loop — thanks everyone. We'll revisit after the canary.
